title: Chains that fold into jobs
question: How does a simple chain of amino acids end up doing a job inside a cell?
hook: Every muscle fibre, enzyme and shield in your body started out as a string of the same few building blocks.
idea: A protein is a chain of amino acids whose sequence, set by a gene, folds it into a shape that fits its job, and the cell later breaks it down and recycles it.

beats.prompt: A mammalian cell makes a new protein. About how long will it last, on average, before the cell breaks it down and recycles it?

choices.label: Only a few seconds
choices.feedback: Some proteins do last only minutes, but the average is far longer than seconds.

choices.label: Many decades, as long as the cell lives
choices.feedback: Proteins are not kept forever; the cell degrades and recycles them.

beats.explain: Proteins exist for a certain period and are then degraded and recycled, with an average lifespan of 1–2 days in mammalian cells.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the history of protein research in order.
items: Gluten is first separated from wheat
Fourcroy recognizes three varieties of animal protein
Mulder describes proteins and Berzelius names them
Hofmeister and Fischer show proteins are chains of amino acids
beats.explain: Gluten was separated around 1747, Fourcroy sorted animal proteins in 1789, proteins were described and named in 1838, and the chain idea came in 1902.

beats.prompt: Match each protein to its job in the cell.
beats.explain: Proteins build structure and also run the cell machinery that marks and removes other proteins.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A linear chain of amino acid residues is called a polypeptide.
A protein contains at least one long polypeptide.
So every polypeptide, however short, counts as a protein.
That means a chain of 10 residues should be called a protein.
beats.explain: Short polypeptides with fewer than 20–30 residues are rarely considered proteins and are commonly called peptides.
